title: US inflation cooled more than expected in August
summary: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge came in below forecasts for August. The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported the PCE price index rose 0.3% on the month and 3.4% from a year earlier, while core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.2% and 3.0%. Disposable personal income increased 0.3% and consumer spending rose 0.9%, or $190.8 billion, with the personal saving rate at 4.1%. Reuters reported the reading gave the Fed some breathing room, and traders pared back bets on another rate increase at the October meeting.
